claims.statement: Code is grouped by domain (DDD-influenced layout, TES-68) into four layers — app/ thin routes, modules/<domain>/{data,domain,ui} with one module per PRD FR (14 domains, matching the modules/ directory), shared/ as the leaf level, and lib/supabase/ as the external data boundary — and new code goes inside its owning module rather than in a new top-level folder.

No business logic lives in app/ (review-level rule): Server Components fetch through a module's data/ layer and compose module ui/ over shared/ui primitives, which is why the dashboard and billing routes (both under app/(dashboard)/t/[tenantCode]/) import data/, domain/ and ui/ surfaces of several modules side by side.
The import direction app → modules → shared → lib/supabase is ESLint-enforced via import/no-restricted-paths zones in eslint.config.mjs covering the app/, modules/, shared/, and lib/ trees.

Another module's data/ is private to every other module: its public surface is domain/ + ui/, and only app/ may fetch from any module's data/; the lint zones are generated per domain from the 14-entry domains array in eslint.config.mjs.

shared/ is the leaf level and must never import modules/ or app/ (lint-enforced) nor lib/supabase/database.types (README rule): it holds the single-file shared/types.ts UI domain types, props-only shared/ui/ primitives (a shared/ui component that starts reading data or encoding business rules moves to its owning module), shared/vocab.ts (closed TESDA vocabulary that stays in shared/ because consumers live in two modules), and shared/text.ts (pure copy shaping). shared/mocks/ was deleted entirely in the mock-data retirement even though shared/README.md still lists it.

Only module data/ layers (besides lib/supabase itself) may import lib/supabase/database.types.ts; app/, shared/, and modules' ui/ and domain/ are lint-blocked from raw DB row types and must import domain types instead.

Two type families stay deliberately separate: lib/supabase/database.types.ts (raw hand-carried rows — Row/Insert/Update per table, seven Postgres enums, RPC signatures, every Relationships stubbed to []) and hand-written shared/types.ts (UI domain types, with Batch as a hub referencing shapes from six other domains and ScholarRow shaped as the T2MIS terminal-report row, fed from learner_details, rather than a second learner entity). The mappers in module data/ layers are the only seam between them; module-scoped non-cross-domain types (Profile) live in that module's domain/ and reuse shared types rather than inventing a second vocabulary, so components never see a snake_case column or a raw enum value.

Every entity contract follows fetch → map → derive per the reference implementation modules/batches/data/batches.ts: fetch is a typed Supabase query whose rows are scoped by RLS (never manually filtered by tenant in JS), map is a pure DB-row to domain translation, derive computes lifecycle/date helpers.

mapBatchRow is pure (no I/O), exported for unit tests, and marks schema gaps with TODO(contract) defaults so the UI shape stays valid — trainingDays/duration/notes and the compatibility aliases currentDay/totalDays stand in as fixed or nullable-derivable defaults — while billingDeadline now reads the real billing_deadline column with a `?? null` guard so an absent column cannot slip past downstream `!== null` checks, and the aliases are never rendered as a 'Day X of Y' claim.

Every read contract returns a four-state discriminated snapshot: ok (mapped rows + dataAsOf = freshest updated_at + fetchedAt), no-tenant-access, sync-failed (Supabase configured but the query errored or the client construction threw — error string kept server-side), and unconfigured (isSupabaseConfigured() false). Since the mock-data retirement no state substitutes fabricated data: selectBatchesForDisplay returns snapshot.batches only for ok and [] for every other state; unconfigured renders an honest empty state with no banner, sync-failed renders the same empty state plus the sync-failed banner. The throwing getBatches() wrapper converts every non-ok state into an exception.

Modules extend the four-state union only with genuinely distinct outcomes and vary the ok payload per contract: tenancy's ProfileSnapshot adds not-found (authenticated with Clerk but no profiles row yet — webhook raced or failed, 'no access yet' rather than an error), import-export's LearnerImportSnapshot adds validation-failed with errors[] decided before any Supabase client is created (partially valid files return ok with a skipped list), and ActivitySnapshot's ok arm carries hasMore derived by fetching one row beyond the requested limit instead of a count query.

Raw error strings never reach the UI: a real sync failure with zero rows renders a fixed-copy sync-failed screen with a Retry link ('Unable to load data' on the dashboard, "Couldn't reach Supabase" on billing, 'Batch data could not be loaded.' on batch cards), never snapshot.error. The inline DashboardCallouts banner is only reachable with live rows — via a `?state=sync-failed` preview override while the snapshot is still ok — so its `isShowingCachedFallback` branch is the preview case: it appends ' — the figures below may be out of date' only when false.

DB_TO_UI_STAGE in modules/batches/data/batches.ts is a total (non-Partial) enum-bridge map so a new DB enum variant fails compilation until its UI treatment is chosen: training/assessment/billing map to UI train/assess/bill, entre is UI-only with no DB column, completed/blocked map to null and are special-cased by deriveLifecycle (all stages done / no stage active), and normalizeStatus surfaces DB blocked as UI pending.

The total-map bridge convention repeats across data layers — STAGE_TO_UI (documents), ACTION_TO_TONE (activity), DB_TO_UI_ROLE (tenancy, DB profile_role a strict subset of UI UserRole), UI_TO_DB_ROLE (tenancy users.ts, the write-direction bridge), ASSESSMENT_RESULT_TO_UI (learners, pending to '') — while DOCUMENT_ICONS is deliberately a Partial map with a generic fallback because document_key is per-program configured data, not a closed enum.

Because a module's data/ is private, batches.ts hand-duplicates documents.ts's mapper logic (MISSING_DOC, mapDocumentRow, the catalog backfill in mapDocumentsMap/mapDocumentRows), kept in sync by hand rather than imported; activity.ts's toRelativeWhen mirrors batches.ts's toDisplayDate with the same unparseable-date-to-empty-string convention.

Cross-module data needs are satisfied by pass-by-parameter or by importing the other module's public domain/: tenancy's getProfileSnapshot takes the caller's Clerk user id because resolving it is modules/auth/data's private job (the file's own header says so), and modules/batches/domain/alerts.ts, modules/batches/domain/attention.ts, modules/batches/domain/metrics.ts and modules/billing/data/billing.ts import from modules/documents/domain/compliance. Since the mock-data retirement a data/ layer's only shared/ imports are types and pure helpers — billing.ts imports Batch/Tenant/DocumentRequirement from shared/types and nothing else from shared/.

domain/ layers are pure business rules with no I/O (urgencyTier, deriveDashboardMetrics, withTenantAccess) and are unit-tested with fixed as-of dates. shared/ may not re-export module code, so module logic sits in module domain/ layers now: metrics lives in modules/batches/domain/metrics.ts (importing both modules/documents/domain/compliance and batches' own domain/urgency) and the tenant-access fold lives in modules/tenancy/domain/access.ts, importable only because domain/ may cross a module boundary and data/ may not.

The per-module split of shared/types.ts is no longer blocked: RULES rule 16 strikes the old prohibition and CLAUDE.md records the split as unblocked, because the blocker was shared/mocks/seed.ts constructing 11 domain types in a layer that cannot import modules/ — and that dataset is gone. shared/README.md still documents the split as deferred, which is documentation drift; Batch's hub role remains a real design cost of splitting, not a boundary violation.

lib/supabase/ is the external data boundary: server.ts builds an anon-key client and attaches the caller's Clerk session token via the accessToken callback, throwing NO_CLERK_TOKEN_MESSAGE (exported so callers can tell 'not signed in' from 'token rejected') instead of silently querying as anon, which RLS would answer with zero rows and no error; service.ts holds the RLS-bypassing service-role client reserved for server-to-server webhook provisioning, and ordinary write paths (tenancy/users.ts, import-export/learnerImport.ts) deliberately stay on the anon client so RLS decides.
No index barrels exist anywhere — deep imports are the convention (shared/README, CLAUDE.md, RULES rule 13); modules with no code yet hold a README naming their FR and planned contents.

The domains array in eslint.config.mjs (14 entries matching the modules/ directory exactly) is the single source that generates the per-module data/-privacy zones — adding a new module requires adding it there or that module's data/ is not made private to other modules.

Mappers are unit-tested in tests/unit/ against the real generated contract: batches.test.ts derives the module-private join-row fixture shape via Parameters<typeof mapBatchRow>[0] instead of duplicating it, and the tests/ directory sits outside the lint zones so test files may import database.types directly, even though app code may not; real-Supabase RLS/tenant-isolation integration tests are still outstanding.

After any migration, database.types.ts must be regenerated and then affected mappers and domain types updated; migrations are additive and supabase/migrations/20260528160300_create_tenant_scoped_schema.sql is the canonical schema + RLS migration.

The 'no row means missing' document backfill is a data-layer decision (batches.ts and documents.ts seed every catalog requirement with MISSING_DOC, then overlay submitted rows), and a key still absent after backfill means untracked — to be read via modules/documents/domain/compliance.ts, never by indexing the map directly.

Derive-layer sentinels protect downstream math: daysUntil returns Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY for a missing or unparseable date (the 'no known deadline' sentinel that sorts last and never trips urgencyTier, since NaN would silently corrupt sorting and urgency math), toDisplayDate and activity.ts's toRelativeWhen return '' rather than 'Invalid Date', and the sentinel is kept out of printable copy by BatchModal's Number.isFinite check (rendering '—' plus 'no billing deadline recorded').

lib/supabase/database.types.ts is currently hand-maintained rather than regenerated: its header records the ADR-006 additions, batches.rqm_code and the T2MIS/learner_details shapes as written by hand from migrations that are now APPLIED and field-checked against generate_typescript_types, with two deliberate divergences from the generator (create_school's nullable text parameters typed string | null; Args kept as Record<string, never>), and every table's Relationships is stubbed as [] — which, per the header's own note, is the root of the long-standing TS2352 casts on embedded-join rows in activity.ts, batches.ts, tenancy.ts and users.ts, and would very likely be retired by adopting the generator's real Relationships arrays.

getBatchesSnapshot, getProfileSnapshot and getPlatformAdminSnapshot are wrapped in React cache() because app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx and the pages and actions in the route group call them independently within one request: the layout reads the profile for the admin nav row, the Sidebar user card and the school switcher, and resolves platform admin through the boolean isPlatformAdmin() helper (which awaits the same cached snapshot) for the 'Add school' row; tenant-scope.ts caches the same profile read for the segment layout; the schools/new page and its Server Action call getPlatformAdminSnapshot directly. cache() scopes the sharing to that request, so a later navigation re-queries.

no-tenant-access is never produced by a query — RLS reports an unattached caller as a successful empty read — so the route folds it in with withTenantAccess(snapshot, access), which replaces only an ok snapshot so a real sync-failed/unconfigured is never masked, and treats access 'unknown' as no rewrite ('we could not check' must not render as 'you have no school'). The fold lives in modules/tenancy/domain/access.ts precisely because a module's domain/ is its importable surface and another module's data/ is private (rule 8). Scoped office routes fold before rendering and branch to shared/ui/NoTenantAccessState instead of their ordinary empty state, and the /t/<school> segment layout branches no-tenant-access, unknown and not-a-member as three distinct screens before any page runs.

Screen guards follow a fixed order — denied, then sync-failed-with-zero-rows, then no-tenant-access, then empty, then no-results — because both sync-failed and no-tenant-access yield zero rows: checking empty first would swallow the retry banner behind a 'no batches, import one' message, and checking empty before no-tenant-access would offer an action the caller cannot perform. The no-results state comes last and lives in the client island, since it is a fact about filters rather than the snapshot.

Some files live in app/ rather than in a module precisely because they compose several private data/ layers, or because a Server Action is a route-level write entry point: app/(dashboard)/tenant-access.ts joins auth's getAuthUserId with tenancy's getProfileSnapshot (the local token read, not getCurrentUser's Clerk API fetch, since only the id is needed), its sibling tenant-scope.ts does the same join for the /t/<school> route segment, the create-user action in app/(dashboard)/users/new/actions.ts joins tenancy's Postgres write with auth's Clerk invitation, and app/(dashboard)/t/[tenantCode]/actions.ts joins tenancy scope resolution with batches' write and activity's append. Each encodes no business rule — validation and writes are delegated to module domain/ and data/ — and tenant-scope's requireScope is the one refusal it does carry, redirecting a trainer to /trainer on an ok scope only.

The four states are applied selectively, not uniformly: DocumentRequirementsSnapshot deliberately has no no-tenant-access member because the requirement catalog is per-program reference data (an empty catalog means unseeded, not unauthorized), and PlatformAdminSnapshot omits it because the verdict comes from a security-definer RPC about the caller rather than a tenant-scoped table.

Mock-data retirement is a contract change, not just a file deletion: batches.ts and activity.ts record that the MOCK_BATCHES / MOCK_ACTIVITY datasets they used to fall back to were deleted, no read path substitutes fabricated rows, and the remaining mentions are stale comments — shared/README.md still calls mocks/ the unconfigured fallback and isSupabaseConfigured's docblock still says 'silent mock fallback'.

Dashboard metric derivation has a single live home: modules/batches/domain/metrics.ts's deriveDashboardMetrics is a pure function over a Batch[] the caller has already loaded, called by the school dashboard route and by app/(dashboard)/trainer/page.tsx's metrics row, and reused per school by modules/batches/domain/overview.ts for the cross-school view; modules/batches/data/metrics.ts (TES-30, derive-only) no longer exists. Every number is computed from the inputs rather than hardcoded, counts only active (ongoing) batches, and anything without a source is null.

The document-requirement catalog is always passed in as a parameter and the billing route still passes [] today, because the live catalog (program_document_requirements) is scoped per scholarship program while Batch carries no resolvable program id — and the empty catalog is designed to degrade to 'not ready', never to a fabricated pass (packets.ts's requirementsUnavailable guard, readiness.ts's requiredTotal > 0 guard). The dashboard goes further: deriveDashboardMetrics summarizes each active batch's own embedded catalog via summarizeOwnCatalogCompliance, so an empty catalog yields docCompliancePct null rather than a percentage.

Write paths return a discriminated state instead of throwing: a thrown Server Action error reaches the browser as an opaque digest that hides whether anything was written, so the create-user action reports through the discriminated CreateUserFormState union — denied/failed/unconfigured for rejections, invalid (field errors)/assigned/invited/duplicate for outcomes, with the raw sync-failed message console-logged server-side — modules/tenancy/data/users.ts returns UserLookupSnapshot/UserAssignmentSnapshot with a distinct denied state, and importLearnersCsv returns validation-failed/sync-failed/ok; unconfigured means the caller must disable the importer rather than pretend the import ran.

The supabase/migrations/ ledger is the canonical 20260528160300_create_tenant_scoped_schema.sql (schema + RLS, which also idempotently seeds tenants, TWSP/CFSP programs, and the 8-key requirement catalog) plus six additive migrations: 20260705070510 adds the trainer_credentials table with RLS; 20260717054607 is a guarded corrective that copies the lone AKB record out of the hand-made, non-conforming public.tenant (singular) table into the canonical tenants table and drops the rogue table, short-circuiting on databases rebuilt from the history where the table never existed; 20260904120000 adds the user-admin write policies; 20260906114735 — renamed from 20260906130000 to match the version the live database records — adds the ADR-006 school registry and platform-admin RLS + RPCs; 20260906120000 adds the ensure_profile_tenant_membership function that applies an invitation's membership atomically; and 20260910120000 adds the ADR-001 billing domain (seven new tables, additive columns on three existing tables, a widened RLS helper, a closed storage-policy gap — single-shot, deliberately no batches.billing_deadline). The dev fixture 20260831120000_seed_dev_operational_data.sql is no longer in the ledger: it moved to supabase/seeds/ so db tooling cannot apply it to every database including the hosted project (#230), although its DEV- prefixed rows remain present on the live database unrecorded.

modules/documents/domain/compliance.ts (the ADR-004 D6 single home for document-compliance rules) exports two deliberately opposite families: the measurement family (docRecordFor, isDocTracked, isDocOnFile, summarizeDocCompliance, summarizeBatchDocCompliance, criticalRequirements), which excludes untracked keys from numerator and denominator and returns null rather than 0 or 100 when nothing is tracked, and the ADR-004 D4 gate family (blockingDocuments, blockerCount, blockingDocumentNames), which fails closed so an untracked requirement blocks via DocBlockerReason 'untracked' | 'missing' | 'pending' (verified/submitted never block). A batch can therefore measure onFilePct 100 and still be blocked, and DocBlocker.key is internal: FR-06 AC-1 forbids rendering a raw document_key, so screens use the display labels returned by blockingDocumentNames.

tests/unit/doc-blockers.test.ts pins ADR-004 D4 as executable assertions — untracked requirements block, missing/pending block while verified/submitted clear, critical blockers are ordered first, blockerCount agrees with blockingDocuments().count, and blockingDocumentNames leaks no catalog document_key (FR-06 AC-1) — including a dedicated test asserting the gate and measurement families deliberately disagree (the same batch reads onFilePct 100 via summarizeBatchDocCompliance yet blockerCount 1). tests/unit/doc-compliance.test.ts pins the measurement side: untracked excluded from both numerator and denominator, null (unknown) when nothing is tracked, submitted on file but not verified, and the same rules inside deriveDashboardMetrics.

modules/documents/domain/evidencePath.ts is a pure (no I/O) security boundary for the compliance-evidence bucket: buildEvidencePath returns {tenant_id}/{batch_id}/{document_key}/{filename} only after validating tenant and batch ids as anchored UUIDs, document_key shape (lowercase alphanumerics plus _ and -, since keys are per-program configured data), and a filename that must not contain / or backslash, be '.' or '..', contain percent-encoded separators (%2f, %5c, %2e%2e), contain control characters, or exceed 200 characters — returning a discriminated EvidencePathResult instead of throwing. The validation is load-bearing because the bucket's RLS policies authorize every read, insert and update with app_private.can_access_tenant((storage.foldername(name))[1]::uuid): the first path segment is the tenant check, so a separator in any input would shift segments and relocate the object into a different tenant's path. validateEvidenceFile enforces EVIDENCE_MAX_BYTES = 52428800 (inclusive, matching the bucket's file_size_limit in the canonical migration) and a narrow MIME allowlist, and EVIDENCE_REJECTION_COPY gives each rejection reason one fixed user-facing sentence with no identifiers, table names, or emoji.

modules/documents/data/evidence.ts is the documents module's storage write path — the Supabase Storage half around the pure domain/evidencePath.ts: uploadEvidence checks isSupabaseConfigured() first, then validates the file and the path before any bytes are sent (rejected means 'we never sent the bytes'), uploads to the private compliance-evidence bucket with upsert:false so re-submitting evidence appends a new object rather than overwriting one an auditor may already have referenced, and returns the four-state EvidenceUploadResult (ok | rejected | sync-failed | unconfigured) instead of throwing, keeping the real error server-side and offering only fixed copy (UPLOAD_FAILED_MESSAGE) to the UI. getSignedEvidenceUrl re-validates the persisted documents.storage_path text (a plain, unconstrained column) by re-parsing it through the same builder before minting a time-limited signed URL, because the bucket is private and no public-URL path exists or may be added; an error and a missing URL both count as sync-failed so an empty link is never returned as ok. No deleteEvidence is exposed: storage.objects has select/insert/update policies but no DELETE policy for this bucket, so deletion is refused for admins and coordinators too; the fix is a can_manage_tenant-gated policy deferred to the Phase 0.1 migration (#36).

The header of modules/documents/data/evidence.ts flags its storage functions as '⚠️ Unverified as of 2026-09-10': they are written but not exercised because two dashboard toggles (Clerk's Supabase integration and Supabase Third-Party Auth, issue #122) are still unset, so createSupabaseServerClient sends a token Postgres will not accept and every call fails with an RLS denial indistinguishable from a code defect; the file directs that it not be debugged against a live project until #122 is closed.

The ADR-004 D4 gate functions (blockingDocuments/blockerCount/blockingDocumentNames) and the evidence storage path are implemented and unit-tested but not consumed by any screen: the only importer of the gate family is tests/unit/doc-blockers.test.ts, the only importer of evidencePath's functions is modules/documents/data/evidence.ts plus tests/unit/evidence-path.test.ts, and uploadEvidence/getSignedEvidenceUrl are imported by no .tsx file — while the measurement family (summarizeBatchDocCompliance, summarizeOwnCatalogCompliance, docRecordFor, criticalRequirements, requirementCatalogOf) is imported by live screens (TableView, DocumentStatusDonut, DocumentsView, AnalyticsView, the documents route) and by batches'/billing's domain and data layers. The gate and evidence functions must not therefore be described as live screen behavior.

modules/tenancy/data/users.ts exposes a write-side result union that is deliberately distinct from the four-state read snapshot contract rather than a fifth read variant: UserLookupSnapshot returns found | not-registered | sync-failed | unconfigured, and UserAssignmentSnapshot returns assigned (profileId, alreadyMember) | not-registered | denied | sync-failed | unconfigured. denied is drawn from a Postgres 42501 with-check violation or an UPDATE that matched zero rows so an RLS refusal is never reported as sync-failed, and not-registered means 'no profile this caller can see' (the invitation half of the flow, not an error) — the distinction app/(dashboard)/users/new/actions.ts relies on to choose between assigning access and inviting.

learners stays tenant-scoped, so a ULI unique by value is not a ULI unique by row: the same person at two schools is two tenant-scoped rows carrying the same uli, learner_identities (uli primary key, RLS-enabled with no policy and no grant, deliberately unpopulated) is only the planned cross-tenant seam, and 20261111120000 adds the narrower partial unique index learners_tenant_batch_uli_key on (tenant_id, batch_id, uli) where uli is not null — one learner once per batch — alongside the canonical (tenant_id, batch_id, learner_no) uniqueness.

The roster's mutation refusal happens in write paths, not in schema constraints: reconcileWithExisting matches only inside one batch, so a ULI held on a row of another batch in the same school inserts instead of colliding, and validateRows rejects a ULI repeated within the file (Duplicate ULI) before any write, so the partial index is never the thing that fails.

Because the index (tenant_id, batch_id, uli) is partial, it is not a legal on-conflict target for a supabase-js upsert; the import therefore fetches the batch's existing (id, uli) rows, reconciles them in domain/ code, then issues one bulk insert plus one update per matched row (supabase-js has no many-rows/many-values update), and writes on update only the columns the CSV actually filled (…row.details, a Partial keyed by learners column) so re-importing a names-only file cannot blank contact, address or employment detail an earlier T2MIS import recorded.

The import write path takes its tenant from the record rather than the caller: fetchBatchTenant re-reads the batch's tenant_id through an RLS-scoped select, so inserted rows can only target a tenant the caller already had read access to, and every failure (unreadable batch, failed reconciliation read, insert or update error, thrown client) returns sync-failed carrying the raw Postgres message — table, column and constraint names — with the header recording a TODO to map that to user copy at the action boundary (RULES rule 6).

The roster read is paged in a dedicated fetchRosterRows helper — 1000 rows at a time, ordered last_name/first_name/id, stopping on a short page — because the API caps a response and would otherwise silently shorten a large school's export. The qualification/T2MIS facts come from a separate batches query, and any error from either read now fails the snapshot outright: the file no longer special-cases not-migrated codes (42703/PGRST200/PGRST204), on the stated ground that blank qualification cells would be indistinguishable from 'not recorded'. mapTenantRoster skips a row whose batch embed is null, groups the rest under batch_code, and fills t2mis from facts rows with the same batch_code; attachRoster then joins onto Batch.id, which mapBatchRow sets to the human batch_code, and a batch with no roster entry passes through unchanged.

The roster is kept out of the batch snapshot because it carries contact, address and employment columns, and the report route is the surface that must therefore be trainer-denied: it redirects a trainer on resolveTrustedRole (profiles.role only, never the ?role= preview override) before either fetch, and folds both snapshots into one syncFailed condition so a failed roster still raises the banner even though the banner copy only mentions batch data.

Guard ordering composes the status union with the role gate rather than flattening both to "zero rows": /t/<code>/batch-cards folds the access verdict first and then returns the sync-failed callout before NoTenantAccessState before EmptyState, the dashboard's guardState runs denied → syncFailed && batchCount === 0 → noTenantAccess → empty, and the report route resolves its hard trainer redirect before either snapshot is consulted and derives one syncFailed from both snapshots.

The two roster snapshots (LearnersSnapshot, TenantRosterSnapshot) carry no freshness pair: rows are ordered by name and updated_at is not selected back, so the "Data as of" stamp has to come from the batch snapshot alone.

mapLearnerRow holds two mapper conventions worth generalizing: a null column and a not-yet-migrated column both read '' through orEmpty so the report renders blank rather than failing, and age is computed by ageOn(dob, asOf) imported from modules/import-export/domain/t2mis — a cross-module domain/ import — against a caller-supplied asOf so the mapper stays pure; the post-training employmentStatus has no column and stays '' behind a TODO(contract).

database.types.ts's stubbed Relationships is what forces the as-unknown row casts on embedded joins — six of them across activity.ts, batches.ts, learners.ts (the roster page and the facts query) and tenancy.ts/users.ts — and the casts are contained because every one lives in a data/ layer; the file header records adopting the generator's real Relationships as the way to retire them.

The import's domain half is unit-tested but its Supabase half is not: tests/unit/learner-import.test.ts covers CSV quoting, header aliasing, the empty and missing-column gates, a blank assessment result defaulting to pending, missing-name / malformed-ULI / duplicate-ULI rejection, reconcileWithExisting marking a match as an update, and summariseWrites choosing ok/partial/sync-failed from the saved counts — while importLearnersCsv's query-and-write flow has no test.

The tenant-access verdict reaching withTenantAccess is derived by one of two helpers: tenantAccessOf(profile) in modules/tenancy/domain/access.ts, used by a page that already holds a resolved scope, or deriveTenantAccess(profileSnapshot) in modules/tenancy/data/tenancy.ts, used by a route holding a profile snapshot, which maps not-found to 'none' but a failed or unconfigured read to 'unknown'.

A learner CSV spanning more than one batch is rejected in the import's validation phase (validation-failed, 'Import one batch at a time') before any Supabase client is created, so the single-batch scope both the reconciliation read and the insert rely on is established before any network call.

getBatchesSnapshot is wrapped in React cache() and its docblock says the layout and each nested page call it independently in one request; the same request-scoped caching covers the two contracts a single request reaches twice — getProfileSnapshot (from which the layout derives isAdmin via resolveTrustedRole, plus the Sidebar user card's full name and the school switcher's tenants) and getPlatformAdminSnapshot (the layout's boolean isPlatformAdmin() helper plus the schools/new page and its Server Action, which call it directly because they need status-level detail). cache() scopes sharing to the request, so a later navigation re-queries.

tests/unit/tenant-access.test.ts pins the fold's two silent failure modes: deriveTenantAccess must read a missing profile row as 'none' but a failed or unconfigured read as 'unknown', and withTenantAccess must rewrite only an ok snapshot, leaving a real failure untouched.

The per-module data/-privacy zone is written as `target: ./modules/!(${d})/**`, which a module's own data/ file matches, so same-module data/ → data/ imports (e.g. batches.ts importing learners.ts) lint clean and the documented 'another module's data/ is private' rule is effectively a cross-module rule only — the lint zone does not enforce same-module layering, and a reviewer is the guard.

The learner import distinguishes a third failure shape: LearnerImportSnapshot carries `partial` alongside ok, validation-failed, sync-failed and unconfigured, and the pure summariseWrites picks it whenever some rows were saved but a step errored, because the two tables are written in separate requests with no rollback. Detail columns go to learner_details as a per-row upsert of only the filled keys, so a names-only re-import cannot blank earlier T2MIS detail.

Nothing in app/ calls importLearnersCsv yet: ImportCsvModal is a deliberate 'not available yet' overlay holding no sample files or fake results, so the import contract is shipped code with no live caller and shared/mocks/ does not stand in for it.

tests/unit/batches.test.ts does not exercise selectBatchesForDisplay's no-tenant-access case: that block asserts only the ok-with-zero-rows, ok, unconfigured and sync-failed inputs, so the adapter's fourth branch is covered by no test (tenant-access.test.ts pins the fold that produces the status, not the adapter).

The mandated guard order is a convention with no type-level enforcement and no test: each consuming route collapses non-ok statuses into booleans and, inside its zero-row branch, returns the sync-failed callout before NoTenantAccessState before EmptyState, so a mis-order is caught only in review. tests/unit/tenant-access.test.ts pins withTenantAccess's rewrite and pass-through behaviour, but the clause order inside a page is unrendered and unpinned, which is why it heads the failure modes.

Rule 19 is satisfied by structure, not by ordering alone: every office route wraps the fetch in withTenantAccess rather than checking afterwards, so a real sync failure survives as sync-failed even for a caller with no school, and only 'empty' remains reachable ahead of the banner. That is why the guard order is the layer rule 19 warns about — the fold cannot be defeated by a fetch, only by a trimmed clause list.

The /t/[tenantCode] actions.ts write path is the write-side form to copy: validate through a module's domain/, write through its data/, return a discriminated state, never throw. It re-resolves the school from the URL code against the caller's memberships (no tenant id read from the form), re-checks the trusted role via resolveTrustedRole rather than the ?role= preview override, and returns SAVE_FAILED on an unknown scope but DENIED on any other non-ok resolution, so 'could not check' is never reported as a refusal — all defence in depth, since the batches UPDATE policy is the boundary.

A zero-row write means two indistinguishable things, so setBatchRqmCode reports conflict-or-denied — one status for a concurrent edit and an RLS refusal — and the action's copy names both readings ('It may have just been changed by someone else, or you may not have permission. Reload and try again.'). A policy that matched nothing therefore surfaces as a state the form explains, never as an error or a silent success; duplicate comes from Postgres 23505 rather than a pre-check, and a failed post-write activity append degrades to logFailed on the success state.

The action lives in app/ because it composes three modules' private data/ layers (tenancy scope resolution, batches, activity), which cannot import each other — so the Server Action is the write-side mirror of why app/ is the composition root. A single-module write such as importLearnersCsv stays in the module; moving it to app/ buys only the entry-point convention.

withTenantAccess itself makes the 'tidier story' impossible: its docblock and tests state that replacing a non-ok snapshot with the plausible no-school explanation would bury the real error, so it rewrites ok only and leaves sync-failed/unconfigured byte-identical. That is what makes the route, not the fold, the only place the story can still be tidied — by ordering.

Rule 2's line is visible on the write path: resolveRouteScope validates the URL code against the caller's own memberships, then the update is narrowed with .eq('tenant_id', scope.tenantId). Neither grants anything — an admin of another school who guessed the code is refused by the UPDATE policy, and the action's header says the same of its own role check.

app/(dashboard)/trainer/page.tsx computes the KPI row from an unscoped getBatchesSnapshot() — no tenant filter, because RLS already limits batches to those assigned to the caller through can_read_batch — then runs deriveTrainerMetrics, which strips the four billing keys from the object itself rather than typing them away (rule 5). Scope is a selection parameter, present or absent, never authorization.

The zones cover database.types.ts explicitly: the first zone's targets are ./app/**, ./shared/**, ./modules/*/ui/** and ./modules/*/domain/**, so data/ and lib/supabase are exactly what remains, and a ui/ file typing props with a generated Row has re-exported the schema. A red import boundary lint is the diagnostic, and the fix it names is to import the other module's domain/ or ui/ or fetch in app/, not to paste the mapper across.

The learner roster is a deliberately separate data/ contract because it selects contact and employment columns no other screen should load and its route is trainer-denied: the batch snapshot stays the source of the batch list and the 'Data as of' stamp, attachRoster feeds per-scholar data onto those batches, and the report route treats a failed roster as its own banner condition. modules/batches/data/learners.ts is therefore the clean demonstration of the allowed edges — lib/supabase, shared/types and one cross-module domain/ import (ageOn), a lone domain/ helper rather than the import-export module.

The page's extension guidance for a write path says to return a result union, keep raw errors server-side, distinguish denied from sync-failed, name the combined conflict-or-denied state where an RLS refusal and a concurrent change are indistinguishable, validate in the owning module's domain/ before the write, re-resolve the school and role server-side, and place the action in app/ if it touches more than one module's data/.
